issue.title: Class "ProjectFolderSchema" not found in .../MigrationShell.php
issue.body:
There seems to be an issue with how the Migrations plugin uses the SchemaShell. It's possible for the `Config/Schema/schema.php` file to use a different class name depending on name of the root folder for the Cake project. 

If one developer with a root folder named "some_project" uses the `Console/cake Migrations.migration generate -f` command on their system, the Schema file is generated with a class name of "SomeProjectSchema". Another developer with a root folder name of "different_name" will subsequently get an error **"Class 'DifferentNameSchema' could not be found in .../MigrationsShell.php on line 546"**. 

The SchemaShell itself allows you to specify the "app name" that will be used when generating the schema file, but the MigrationShell does not support passing this option through. This leaves developers to edit the class name in schema.php manually to match their project directory whenever this occurs.

body: Would supporting the `--name` argument for `schema generate` solve this?

Sure - if you know about it and if you type it every single time and agreed with everyone in the team to use a specific name. I've already implemented a work-around in the migrations plugin but IMO this is a generic "issue" that should be fixed in the core.

Why was it implemented the way it is, taking the app folders name instead of using a fixed name like "App" that can be optionally changed if you want? Relying on the folder makes it pretty much random.

> Why was it implemented the way it is, taking the app folders name instead of using a fixed name like "App" that can be optionally changed if you want? Relying on the folder makes it pretty much random.

I have no idea. It was done like this in the 1.2 days before I joined the project.
Can we change it or not? I think it would make sense if it is consistent across different installs.
I don't see why we can't change it. Not like the behavior right now is particularly useful. We might want to be careful with how a fixed name would interact with plugins.

It can still use the name of the plugin for plugin-based schemas-- that part is still predictable enough to count on (since the name of the plugin's folder **does** actually get used in code, it can't be changed between installations like APP_DIR might be).

It would probably be wise to implement a fallback though for the time being: At least on the schema _reading_ side of things check for 'AppSchema' first, then `APP_DIR . Schema` in order to maintain backwards compatibility with existing schema.php files. Unless I'm overlooking something, all new _writes_ could use 'AppSchema' by default going forward.
I should qualify that I'm speaking in the context of the base Cake app. The logic for prepending the Plugin name (if present) should probably remain as is.

> It would probably be wise to implement a fallback though for the time being: At least on the schema reading side of things check for 'AppSchema' first, then APP_DIR . Schema in order to maintain backwards compatibility with existing schema.php files. Unless I'm overlooking something, all new writes could use 'AppSchema' by default going forward.

Sound like a good solution to me! :+1:

There is a related issue with the SchemaShell here: 

https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/92957913d93404d8554345d4e41cb3c723a0a842/lib/Cake/Console/Command/SchemaShell.php#L74,L76

This condition makes it impossible to tell SchemaShell that you want to use a custom `--name` for the schema class, but still with the default `--file schema.php`.

issue.title: Bug/schema naming
issue.body:
Proposed fix for CakeDC/migrations#131.

Adds an option for specifying the Schema class name on the command line.

Updates `_getSchema()` and `_updateSchema()` to use a new `_getSchemaClassName()` method, which merges existing behavior for plugins with a new default for base Cake applications.

Most importantly, `Config/Schema/schema.php` files will now be generated using `AppSchema` as the default class name instead of `APP_DIR . 'Schema'`.

Thanks to @burzum for the initial attempt at resolving this.

body: Well the code can be changed :smile:
Sure. That was my plan. I ran out of time yesterday though and just wanted to get it documented so _I_ could remember what to do later. Thanks.

body:
Okay, so @markstory, the conditional I linked to on Friday was added by you to fix #2202. Here's the description for that PR:

> Fix file always being set to 'schema.php'
> 
> When the name parameter is set and no custom file value is provided,
> the name should be used to generate the file name. empty() cannot be
> used because the file parameter has a default value of 'schema.php'.

I wanted to avoid completely undoing this previous fix and just trading one problem off for another. My approach is to modify the logic so that if `params[file]` is explicitly set, that will **always** be used, even if it matches the default filename. The only practical way to differentiate between the option parser using the default value vs one actually provided by the user is to remove the parser's default value (which should be okay since startup() will _always_ set a filename.)

This is a little unrelated, but seeing as I just wasted Travis's time building a PR with a missing paren in it, I was wondering how the core team does local testing on things that really require a "set up" Cake app.

I was (clearly) being lazy because I didn't want to set my fork up with a DB connection and composer installs and vagrant and fake db tables and models to work with in order to actually **run** the SchemaShell locally, but obviously you guys can't get away with that day to day. How do you handle that, and is it something easy for contributors to use as well?
When I need to load schema files with custom names I combine the `file` and `name` options in the command line to load the desired file

@lorenzo The problem is that you can't use a custom `--name` with **the default** `--file` argument. If you tried to specify `bin/cake schema generate --name brian --file schema.php` you would end up with a file named `Config/Schema/brian.php` instead of `schema.php` as expected. The PR fixes that.
